question: Where should AI in the cockpit go first?
results: 40% said maintenance and documents, 20% said pilot decision support, 40% said AI should be kept out of the cockpit

question: What's the biggest barrier to AI adoption in aviation ops?
results: 16% said regulatory certification timelines, 20% said operator trust and culture, 23% said data quality & integration, 41% said liability & accountability

question: What's the biggest barrier to commercial eVTOL launch?
results: 27% said aircraft certification, 37% said traffic management infrastructure, 20% said public trust & adoption, 17% said airport/vertiport access

question: Where does flight data analytics deliver the most value today?
results: 59% said fuel efficiency and savings, 5% said pilot performance feedback, 24% said safety and risk monitoring, 11% said maintenance and reliability

question: Where will AI have the biggest safety impact in aviation?
results: 17% said preflight planning & briefing, 17% said ATC flow & conflict management, 14% said cockpit decision support, 52% said maintenance & anomaly detection

question: Where is the biggest operational data blind spot in aviation today?
results: 53% said ground and ramp operations, 31% said aircraft parts & MRO, 4% said terminal & passenger flow, 12% said crew & staff movement

question: What's the biggest hurdle to commercial electric regional aviation?
results: 27% said aircraft certification, 20% said charging infrastructure, 7% said ops and dispatch software, 45% said economic viability at scale

question: Who builds the best flight ops software?
results: 46% said dedicated industry vendors, 38% said airlines building in-house, 13% said big tech cloud providers, 4% said aviation AI startups
vincent_note: The 4% for aviation AI startups shows the industry is still heavily skeptical of AI-native players despite the hype — a meaningful contrast worth referencing in AI adoption discussions.
